+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: Give the JSCInterpreter watchdog a clock seam, and remove the real-clock watchdog checks
+---
+## What
+The user decision on ^tm4x2hp and ^kdtrmhv is: "no test checks the speed of the machine". The `JSCInterpreter` watchdog has no clock seam. Thus these tests still depend on a real watchdog time:
+
+- `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/HardeningTests.swift` `executionTimeLimitBoundaryAllowsAFastSnippet`: a 0.3 s watchdog must not fire. A slow machine can make it fire.
+- `HardeningTests.cancellationStressTestNoDeadlock`: a 10 s watchdog.
+- About 45 tests that use the default 5 s watchdog of `JSCInterpreter`. A slow machine can end a snippet that is correct.
+- The dry-run time limits in `SampleSnippetTests`, `SearchToolsToolTests` and `MCPCapabilityTests`.
+
+^kdtrmhv used `unreachedTimeLimit` (86_400 s) for the tests that it changed. That is a stopgap, not a seam.
+
+## Do
+- Add an injected clock (or an event seam) for the watchdog of `JSCInterpreter`. The production default stays the real clock.
+- Convert each test above: a test of the watchdog opens the clock. Every other test uses a clock that does not end.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] No root test depends on the real time of the watchdog.
+- [ ] The watchdog tests prove the watchdog fires, by an event, not by a duration.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Root `swift test` passes once.
\ No newline at end of file

+  text: |-
+    Research done.
+    - The watchdog lives in `WatchdogState` (JSCInterpreter.swift). JSC calls `shouldTerminate()` each 20 ms poll on the JS thread, and `pumpUntilSettled` calls it while it waits. The deadline check is `runStart.duration(to: .now) >= .seconds(timeLimit)` on `ContinuousClock`. This check is synchronous, thus a `Clock` cannot replace it directly: `GatedClock.now` moves only when a sleep on it ends.
+    - Plan: a `WatchdogDeadline` that sleeps until the deadline on an injected `any Clock<Duration>` (a stored timer Task, cancelled at teardown) and marks the deadline as an event. It also compares `clock.now` with the deadline, as the backstop when no thread of the cooperative pool is free to run the timer. Default clock: `ContinuousClock`. `withTimeLimit(_:)` keeps the clock, thus `MultiTool` keeps an injected clock.
+    - `MultiTool` runs `interpreter.run` on `DispatchQueue.global`, not on the cooperative pool.
+    - Tests in scope: HardeningTests (cancellation tests with 86_400 s, stress test with 10 s, the four executionTimeLimit boundary tests), JSCInterpreterTests (default 5 s, `unreachedTimeLimit`, 1.0/0.3/10/30 s), MetricsTests (0.2 s and default), TypedMockDryRunTests (0.5 s and default), CoreLogRecordTests, ResultRendererTests, SampleSnippetTests, SearchToolsToolTests, MCPCapabilityTests.
+    - `GatedClock` is in the unit test target only. The integration package does not compile it.

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m3x83v8j82qxwtx766sg4mjb
+  text: |-
+    Implementation landed.
+    - Seam: `JSCInterpreter.init(timeLimit:watchdogClock:)` (internal). The public `init(timeLimit:)` forwards with `ContinuousClock()`, thus production behavior does not change. `withTimeLimit(_:)` keeps the clock, thus `MultiTool.init` keeps an injected clock.
+    - New private `WatchdogDeadline` in JSCInterpreter.swift: a stored timer Task sleeps on the clock until the deadline and marks it; each check also compares `clock.now` with the deadline (the backstop when the cooperative pool has no free thread). `Sandbox.tearDown()` calls `WatchdogState.disarm()`, which cancels the timer. `WatchdogState.runStart`/`timeLimit` are replaced by `deadline`. The doc in MultiToolConfiguration.swift now names `deadline`.
+    - Test support: `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/Support/JSCInterpreter+HeldWatchdog.swift` adds `JSCInterpreter.makeWithHeldWatchdog(timeLimit:)` (a `GatedClock` that nothing opens).
+    - Watchdog tests open a `GatedClock` and check the outcome and `recordedSleeps`: JSCInterpreterTests `infiniteLoopTerminatedByWatchdog`, `withTimeLimitReturnsAnInterpreterArmedWithTheGivenLimit`; HardeningTests four `executionTimeLimit*` boundary tests; MetricsTests `timedOutRunRecordsTimedOut`; TypedMockDryRunTests `nonTerminatingSnippetFails`.
+    - Every other listed test uses the held watchdog: all `JSCInterpreter()` runs and `unreachedTimeLimit` (86_400 s) uses in JSCInterpreterTests, the three HardeningTests cancellation tests (stress test now has a hang guard), CoreLogRecordTests, MetricsTests, ResultRendererTests, TypedMockDryRunTests, SampleSnippetTests, SearchToolsToolTests, MCPCapabilityTests (`dryRunTimeLimit` removed). `syntaxCheckExecutesNothing` now has a hang guard.
+    - What did not work: the first run asserted `recordedSleeps` right after a fast run that the closed clock did not end. The timer Task can start after the run returns, so the list was empty. Fix: HardeningTests `expectArmed` waits for the event "a sleep is recorded" with `TestPoll.waitUntil`, then checks the duration.
+    - Note: `MultiTool` instances that inject no interpreter still arm the 120 s default ceiling on the real clock. No root test reaches it, and the card did not list those tests. `ToolAPIRendererTests` calls only `checkSyntax`, which arms no watchdog.
